question: Should the experimental Claws lifecycle become a durable owner of entries in OpenClaw's existing global MCP registry under the contract proposed by the open RFC?
rationale: This choice introduces persistent ownership, cleanup authority, recovery obligations, and executable or remote capability installation in core; code review cannot accept that product boundary while the RFC remains open.

options.title: Defer Pending RFC
options.body: Keep this draft open and unmerged until the RFC and prerequisite stack are accepted, then review the implementation against the approved ownership contract.

options.title: Approve Direct Ownership
options.body: Sponsor direct Claw ownership of existing MCP registry entries and require complete coexistence, recovery, consent, upgrade, and proof gates before landing.

options.title: Remove MCP Ownership
options.body: Exclude MCP registry mutation from the initial Claws lifecycle and rely on separately installed bundle or plugin configuration.

recommendation.title: Defer Pending RFC
recommendation.body: Keep this draft open and unmerged until the RFC and prerequisite stack are accepted, then review the implementation against the approved ownership contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned reviewer and have already supplied the detailed product and persistence review that shaped this implementation.
